 Fatima Sana Calls for Equal Treatment in Pakistan
 By Arooj Fatima 
 | Published Nov 11, 2026 | 6:23 pm 
 -->
 Pakistan women’s cricket team captain Fatima Sana has called for equal treatment of men’s and women’s cricket in the country, urging fans to show greater support for female players by attending their matches.
 The 25-year-old said she hopes to see a time when Pakistan’s women’s team receives the same recognition and support as the men’s team.
 ALSO READ 
 Pakistan Qualify for for SAFF Championship 2026 Semifinals 
 Speaking to CricBlog TV after Perth Scorchers’ six-wicket victory over Melbourne Stars on Sunday, Sana said cricket is growing worldwide and expressed hope that women’s cricket would see similar progress in Pakistan.
 She also urged fans to attend women’s matches in the same numbers as men’s games.
 Sana, who has captained Pakistan since 2024, is currently representing Perth Scorchers in Australia’s Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL), one of the leading women’s cricket competitions.
 The right-arm medium-fast bowler is the second Pakistani player to compete in the WBBL, following former captain Nida Dar, who represented Sydney Thunder in 2019.
 Since making her WBBL debut on October 31, Sana has taken five wickets in five matches at an economy rate of 7.62 runs per over, placing her joint 10th among the tournament’s leading wicket-takers.
 This is Sana’s second appearance in an overseas cricket league, having previously represented Birmingham Phoenix in England’s The Hundred competition.
 She expressed appreciation for the opportunity to play in Australia and praised her Perth Scorchers teammates for their support. She currently plays alongside former New Zealand captain Sophie Devine and Australian batter Beth Mooney.
 Sana also expressed hope that more Pakistani women cricketers would get opportunities to compete in Australia, helping them gain experience and contribute to the growth of women’s cricket back home.

 The Pakistan captain holds the world record for the fastest half-century in women’s T20 internationals and led her country to a bronze medal at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
 Meanwhile, Pakistan is scheduled to host the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup in 2028, featuring 12 teams. It will be the country’s first ICC women’s tournament.
 Pakistan has previously hosted two men’s ODI World Cups and the ICC Men’s Champions Trophy in 2025.
 Sana welcomed the decision to hold the tournament in Pakistan, saying it could encourage more girls to take up cricket.
 She believes that watching international women’s cricket at home could also encourage parents to provide more opportunities for their daughters to participate in the sport.
